transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (Redwood Partnerships), Jonas (CTO, HelixCloud), Priya (Head of AI), Markus (Cloud Architect), Sofia (Partnerships)

Summary/Notes (auto): brief intro, product overview from Redwood, HelixCloud capability summary, integration models discussed, security & compliance check, next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Maya from Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on the partner program, with me today is Ethan our solutions engineer and Lina on partner ops. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Jonas: good, thanks, Jonas here. excited to learn more, we chatted over email but wanted to dig into how Redwood thinks about partner integrations.
[00:14] Maya: great, quick agenda, high level partner models (resell, refer, integration), a bit about Redwood's runtime and dedicated/private options, and then open Qs for HelixCloud, ok? sound good?
[00:24] Priya: yep sounds good, we have about 50 minutes.
[00:28] Ethan: I'll jump in on the technical bits, but to start real quick, Redwood is a developer-first inference platform - hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private VPC/on-prem options. we do batching, KV cache, runtime kernels that pick quantized execution paths, etc.
[00:42] Markus: when you say dedicated, is that like reserved GPUs that you manage and we resell, or customers spin up under our tenancy?
[00:49] Maya: good q - partnership models vary. resell model: Redwood provides dedicated clusters we can inventory under a partner SKU and you resell. integration model: we enable Helix to run our control plane in a partner-managed VPC / private deployment, that gives you more operational control and billing under your account. we can also do hybrid - hosted control plane with private data plane.
[01:09] Jonas: ok, hybrid sounds interesting. a lot of our enterprise customers ask for VPC or customer-managed networking because of data residency and audit. we also have customers that want a white-labeled managed inference product.
[01:20] Lina: we have a partner kit for white-label - includes docs, pricing guidance, and integration checklists, we'll share it after the call.
[01:27] Priya: on the tech side, what's typical latency / throughput on a dedicated pool for e.g. a 13B model? our customers care about p95 latency and cost/unit.
[01:36] Ethan: practical numbers depend on hardware and quantization. on modern A100/H100 class hardware we see single-request p95 for 13B models in the 120-220ms range with optimized kernels and continuous batching; throughput depends on batch size and concurrency - dedicated pools can do hundreds of concurrent requests with right autoscaling. smaller GPUs or lower perf instances will be higher. also caching (prefix/KV) reduces repeated context cost. these are ballpark; we should run a bench with your workload.
[02:03] Markus: do you support multi-tenant isolation within a dedicated cluster? we need strict isolation for enterprise customers.
[02:08] Ethan: yes - we support tenant isolation via namespace-level quotas, per-tenant model pinning, and network level policies in private deployments. for Dedicated (Redwood-managed), we provide isolation at the runtime and container boundary and optional per-customer VPC peering.
[02:24] Jonas: security/compliance - SOC2 is table stakes, also SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integration. do you have HSM/KMS support?
[02:33] Maya: we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs in Console, and KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private deployments; HSM options on Private via customer KMS/HSM are supported. we can share our security pack.
[02:43] Priya: great, we'll need the SOC2 report and network architecture for any pilot.
[02:48] Maya: absolutely, will attach SOC2 artifact and security deck after.
[02:52] Sofia: business model - commissions, margin, partner discounts? how do you price partner-resold dedicated capacity?
[02:59] Maya: partner pricing depends on commitment size. typical partner discounts for reseller are X% off list at various tiers (we'll send the sheet). For pilots we can offer free credits or a discounted pilot rate. Long-term we support co-terming and metered billing under partner SKUs.
[03:15] Jonas: what's the operational model for rollouts / model versioning? we need canary, A/B, rollbacks.
[03:21] Ethan: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and A/B, pinned model versions, automatic fallback to compatible variants if a version fails. we also emit traces and token-level latency/cost breakdown. you can configure automatic fallback policies by route.
[03:36] Markus: that fallback - does it work across different model architectures? like fall back from a large 70B to a 13B tuned variant?
[03:42] Ethan: yes, compatible variants concept. you can specify acceptable fallbacks; the runtime will re-route to a compatible smaller model when capacity constrained. prompt/response differences are fuzzy but you can configure quality-regression alerts.
[03:56] Priya: for benchmarks - what do you need from us to run a meaningful perf test?
[04:00] Ethan: typical ask: sample prompt set or synthetic distribution (sequence length distribution), expected concurrency/qps, target p95 SLA, models to test, and if possible a small dataset that represents production prompts. we'll also want infra details - instance types, network, and any encryption in flight constraints.
[04:18] Jonas: we can share an anonymized prompt set and our typical concurrency profile. also curious about quantization support - do you recommend int8/4 for production?
[04:27] Ethan: quantization recommendations depend on model and workload. some 13B models are robust to int8 with small quality delta; for high-regulated customers we tend to recommend validated quant profiles and run evals against your ground truth to measure regressions. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles by workload.
[04:47] Sofia: commercial parity question - if we resell, do you allow white-labeling of console or must Redwood Console be visible?
[04:54] Maya: white-label options exist on partner tiers; for Private deployments you can host your own control plane which can be branded. for Redwood-managed Dedicated resell, we support co-branded partner portals. we'll share partner kit details.
[05:06] Markus: networking question - if we do private data plane in our VPC, what's the control plane connectivity requirement?
[05:12] Ethan: there are two models: control plane hosted (Redwood) communicates to your VPC endpoints over peered network or secure tunnel; or we deploy control plane images into your control plane (private) - in that case it's all internal. for the hybrid we need egress ports for health checks and telemetry. we'll give specifics in the integration checklist.
[05:32] Priya: any limits on model catalog? can Helix add partner-specific model variants or private models?
[05:37] Ethan: yes - private model upload and pinning is supported on Private deployments; for Hosted we support partner-private models as well with access controls. integration with model registries is available via APIs.
[05:46] Jonas: for pilot customers who are regulated, audit logs and retention are key. can we configure audit retention windows?
[05:52] Maya: yes, retention windows for logs and transcripts are configurable for Dedicated/Private; hosted defaults are configurable at enterprise plan.
[05:59] Sofia: competitive landscape - we hear from customers about CoreWeave and Lambda offering similar things. how do you position Redwood?
[06:05] Maya: we emphasize production-grade runtime + unified API across hosted/dedicated/private; our differentiator is the orchestration (smart routing, KV/prefix caching, and clear cost controls), plus partner enablement - onboarding, benchmarks, and co-selling. we'll send a short competitive one-pager.
[06:22] Jonas: sounds good. operationally, what does a pilot look like? timeline?
[06:26] Lina: typical pilot 4-6 weeks: week 0 planning and infra prep, week 1-2 perf tests and tuning, week 3 pilot with a subset of customers, week 4 wrap and handoff. we can compress depending on availability.
[06:40] Markus: onboarding checklist - who from our side is needed?
[06:44] Maya: infra contact (you're Markus), security/compliance (Jonas or delegated), product/owner for integration tests (Priya), and partnership/legal for agreements (Sofia).
[06:55] Priya: for benchmarks I'd like Redwood to run an evaluation against our ground truth to measure quality regression after quantization. is that standard?
[07:02] Ethan: yep we can run evals and produce quality/regression metrics tied to prompt sets. Redwood Optimize ties evals to alerts for regressions.
[07:12] Jonas: any blockers legally - we should exchange a standard MSA/NDA early.
[07:16] Lina: we'll share our partner MSA template; if you have an NDA/partner agreement, please send it.
[07:22] Maya: ok quick recap and next steps - we'll send partner intro deck, pricing, SOC2/security pack, and propose technical deep-dive times. Helix to share infra diagram and sample prompt set. action owners noted in the doc.
[07:34] Sofia: thank you, this was helpful.
[07:36] Jonas: thanks, look forward to the deep dive.
[07:40] Maya: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and post links to shared artifacts (deck + partner kit).
